title: T-Count Study: 8 Gates
lesson: The best check strategy depends on which paths remain legal.
brief: This version contains four T gates and four T† gates. You still have only two checks. Find the strongest layout you can while meeting the Yield target, then compare it with the earlier circuits.
learning_moment: The T gates restrict check propagation, but T count is not the only thing that determines the score. Circuit depth, gate locations, the errors the checks can detect, and the noise model all matter. Compare the best layout you found across the full 0/2/4/8 series, and report both Fidelity and Yield. A higher Fidelity by itself is not a fair comparison if it keeps far fewer runs. The T-COUNT STUDY printout lists the series side by side.
hint: Use the earlier T-count results as a baseline. Do not just add checks: look for legal spans that catch the dominant phase-flip errors without sacrificing too much Yield.
reflection: Across the series, what changed in legal check placements, Fidelity, and Yield? What else changed besides T count?
noise_note: Most modeled errors are phase flips (Z errors).

noise.label: dephasing-dominated (Z-biased) level noise, same for the whole series

explanation: With eight T and T† gates, an X check is blocked almost everywhere.
The last CNOT between q0 and q1 comes after every T gate, so a short check from slot 8, X on q0 and q1, can watch it for phase flips.
The other check, Z on q3 across the whole circuit, sees no phase flips at all. It helps another way: it ends at the readout, so it asks whether q3 is still 0 and catches readout flips on q3.
Compare the whole series with the T-COUNT STUDY printout.
